cues.en: Let's dive into artificial neural networks and how they work at a high level.
cues.zh: 從高層次深入人工神經網路，以及它如何運作。

cues.en: Later on, we'll actually get our hands dirty and actually create some, but first we need to understand how they work and where they came from.
cues.zh: 稍後會動手實際建立，但首先要了解運作方式與起源。

cues.en: It's pretty amazing stuff.
cues.zh: 這些內容非常驚人。

cues.en: This whole field of artificial intelligence is based on an understanding of how our own brains work.
cues.zh: 整個人工智慧領域，是建立在對人腦運作的理解之上。

cues.en: Over millions of years of evolution, nature has come up with a way to make us think, and if we just reverse engineer the way that our brains work, we can gain some insights on how to make machines that think.
cues.zh: 經過數百萬年演化，大自然想出了讓我們思考的方法；只要反向研究大腦如何運作，就能得到啟發，製造會思考的機器。

cues.en: Within your brain, specifically within your cerebral cortex, which is where all of your thinking happens, you have a bunch of neurons.
cues.zh: 大腦中，尤其是進行思考的大腦皮質，有很多神經元。

cues.en: These are individual nerve cells, and they are connected to each other by axons and dendrites.
cues.zh: 它們是個別神經細胞，透過軸突與樹突彼此連接。

cues.en: You can think of these as connections, wires, if you will, that connect different axons together.
cues.zh: 可以把它們想成連線或電線，將不同軸突連接起來。

cues.en: Now, an individual neuron will fire or send a signal to all of the neurons that it's connected to when enough of its input signals are activated.
cues.zh: 當足夠多的輸入訊號被啟動時，單個神經元就會放電，向所有與它連接的神經元發出訊號。

cues.en: At the individual neuron level, it's a very simple mechanism: you just have this neuron that has a bunch of input signals coming into it, and if enough of those inputs signals reach a certain threshold, it will in turn
cues.zh: 在單一神經元層次，機制很簡單：有多個輸入訊號，只要足夠多的輸入達到某個門檻，它就會

cues.en: fire off a set of signals to the neurons that it in turn is connected to as well.
cues.zh: 向與它連接的其他神經元發送一組訊號。

cues.en: But when you start to have many, many, many of these neurons connected together in many, many different ways with different strengths between each connection, things get very complicated.
cues.zh: 但當非常多神經元，以許多不同方式連接，而且每個連線強度不同時，事情就很複雜。

cues.en: This is a perfect example of "emergent behavior."
cues.zh: 這是「湧現行為」的完美例子。

cues.en: You have a very simple concept, a very simple model, but when you stack enough of them together, you can create very complex behavior that can yield learning behavior.
cues.zh: 概念與模型非常簡單，但堆疊足夠多，就能產生非常複雜、甚至能學習的行為。

cues.en: This actually works.
cues.zh: 這真的有效。

cues.en: Not only does it work in your brain, it works in our computers as well.
cues.zh: 不只在人腦有效，在電腦裡也有效。

cues.en: Now think about the scale of your brain.
cues.zh: 想想大腦的規模。

cues.en: You have billions of neurons, each of them with thousands of connections.
cues.zh: 有數十億個神經元，每個都有數千個連接。

cues.en: That's what it takes to actually create a human mind.
cues.zh: 這才造就人類心智。

cues.en: And this is a scale that we can still only dream about in the field of Deep Learning and Artificial Intelligence, but it's the same basic concept.
cues.zh: 這個規模，在深度學習與人工智慧領域，仍只能夢想，但基本概念相同。

cues.en: You just have a bunch of neurons with a bunch of connections that individually behave very simply, but once you get enough of them together wired in enough complex ways, you can actually create
cues.zh: 就是很多神經元，加上很多連線，個別行為很簡單，但只要以夠複雜的方式，連接足夠多神經元，就能產生

cues.en: very complex thoughts, and even consciousness.
cues.zh: 非常複雜的思考，甚至意識。

cues.en: The plasticity of your brain is basically tuning where those connections go to and how strong each one is, and that's where all the magic happens.
cues.zh: 大腦的可塑性，基本上就是調整連線接到哪裡，以及每條連線有多強，神奇之處都在這裡。

cues.en: Furthermore, if we look deeper into the biology of your brain, you can see that within your cortex neurons seem to be arranged into stacks or cortical columns that process information in parallel.
cues.zh: 進一步研究腦部生物學，會發現皮質中的神經元，似乎排列成堆疊或皮質柱，平行處理資訊。

cues.en: So, for example, in your visual cortex different areas of what you might see might be getting processed in parallel by different columns, or cortical columns, of neurons.
cues.zh: 例如，在視覺皮質中，看到的不同區域，可能由不同神經元柱或皮質柱，平行處理。

cues.en: Each one of these columns is in turn made up of mini-columns of around 100 neurons per mini-column.
cues.zh: 每個柱又由微柱組成，每個微柱約有 100 個神經元。

cues.en: Mini-columns are then organized into larger hyper-columns, and within your cortex there are about 100 million of these mini-columns.
cues.zh: 微柱再組成更大的超柱，皮質中大約有一億個這樣的微柱。

cues.en: So again, they just add up very quickly.
cues.zh: 所以，數量很快就累積起來。

cues.en: Coincidentally, this is a similar architecture to how the 3D video card in your computer works.
cues.zh: 巧合的是，這與電腦 3D 顯示卡的架構相似。

cues.en: It has a bunch of very simple, very small processing units that are responsible for computing how little groups of pixels on your screen are computed.
cues.zh: 顯示卡有很多非常簡單、微小的處理單元，負責計算螢幕上一小組像素。

cues.en: It just so happens that that's a very useful architecture for mimicking how your brain works.
cues.zh: 剛好，這種架構很適合模仿大腦運作。

cues.en: So it's sort of a happy accident that the research behind your favorite video games lent itself to the same technology that made Artificial Intelligence possible on a grand scale and at low cost.
cues.zh: 所以是個幸運的巧合：你最喜愛的電玩背後的研究，促成了能以低成本、大規模實現人工智慧的同一種技術。

cues.en: The same video cards you're using to play your video games can also be used to perform Deep Learning and create artificial neural networks.
cues.zh: 玩電玩用的同一張顯示卡，也能執行深度學習、建立人工神經網路。

cues.en: Think about how much better it would be if we actually made chips that were purpose-built specifically for simulating artificial neural networks.
cues.zh: 想想，如果製造專門模擬人工神經網路的晶片，會更好多少。

cues.en: Well, it turns out some people are designing chips like that right now.
cues.zh: 其實，現在確實有人在設計這樣的晶片。

cues.en: By the time you watch this they might even be a reality.
cues.zh: 等你看到這裡，可能已經成真。

cues.en: I think Google's working on one as we speak.
cues.zh: 我想，Google 現在就正在研究。

cues.en: So at one point, someone said, "Hey!
cues.zh: 因此，某個時候，有人說：「嘿，

cues.en: "The way we think neurons work is pretty simple.
cues.zh: 我們認為神經元的運作方式，很簡單。

cues.en: "It actually wouldn't be too hard "to actually replicate that ourselves "and maybe try to build our own brain."
cues.zh: 自己複製它，其實不會太難，也許可以試著建立自己的大腦。」

cues.en: This idea goes all the way back to 1943.
cues.zh: 這個想法最早可以追溯到 1943 年。

cues.en: People proposed a very simple architecture where if you have an artificial neuron, maybe you can set up an architecture where that neuron fires only if more than a certain number of its input connections are active.
cues.zh: 人們提出非常簡單的架構：一個人工神經元，只有在超過一定數量的輸入連線啟動時，才會放電。

cues.en: When they thought about this more deeply in a computer science context, people realized you can actually create logical expressions, or boolean expressions, by doing this.
cues.zh: 從資訊科學角度深入思考後，人們發現，這樣其實能建立邏輯運算式或布林運算式。

cues.en: Depending on the number of connections coming from each input neuron, and whether each connection activates or suppresses a neuron, you can actually implement logical expressions in artificial or natural neurons.
cues.zh: 依據每個輸入神經元的連線數，以及每條連線是啟動還是抑制神經元，就能在人工或自然神經元中，實作邏輯運算式。

cues.en: This particular diagram is implementing an OR operation, so imagine that our threshold for our neuron was that if you have two or more inputs active, you will in turn fire off a signal.
cues.zh: 這張圖實作 OR 運算。假設神經元門檻是：至少有兩個輸入啟動，就發出訊號。

cues.en: In this setup here, we have two connections to neuron A and two connections coming in from neuron B.
cues.zh: 這裡的設定，從神經元 A 有兩條連線，從神經元 B 也有兩條連線。

cues.en: If either of those neurons produce an input signal, that will actually cause neuron C to fire, so you can see we have created an OR relationship here where if either a neuron A or neuron B
cues.zh: 任一神經元產生輸入訊號，就會讓神經元 C 放電。因此建立了 OR 關係：只要 A 或 B

cues.en: feeds neuron C two input signals, that will cause neuron C to fire and produce a "true" output.
cues.zh: 向 C 提供兩個輸入訊號，就會讓 C 放電，產生 true 輸出。

cues.en: We've implemented here the boolean operation C = A OR B just using the same wiring that happens within your own brain.
cues.zh: 我們只是用與腦內相同的接線方式，就實作了布林運算 C = A OR B。

cues.en: It's also possible to implement AND and NOT via similar means.
cues.zh: 用類似方式，也能實作 AND 與 NOT。

cues.en: Then we start to build upon this idea.
cues.zh: 接著，在這個想法上繼續發展。

cues.en: We created something called the Linear Threshold Unit, or LTU for short, in 1957.
cues.zh: 1957 年，建立了稱為線性門檻單元的東西，簡稱 LTU。

cues.en: This just built on things by assigning weights to those inputs, so instead of just simple ON and OFF switches, we now have the concept of having weights on each of those inputs as well.
cues.zh: 它在原本概念上，替輸入指定權重，因此不只是簡單的開關，也有每個輸入的權重概念。

cues.en: This is working more toward our understanding of the biology; different connections between different neurons may have different strengths, and we can model those strengths in terms of these weights
cues.zh: 這更接近我們對生物學的理解：不同神經元之間的連線，可能有不同強度，可以用人工神經元

cues.en: on each input coming into our artificial neuron.
cues.zh: 各個輸入的權重，模擬這些強度。

cues.en: We're also going to have the output be given by a step function.
cues.zh: 輸出則由階躍函數決定。

cues.en: So this is similar in the spirit into how we were using it before, but instead of saying we're going to fire if a certain number of inputs are active, well, there's no concept anymore
cues.zh: 精神上與先前相似，但不再說一定數量輸入啟動就放電，因為現在沒有

cues.en: of active or not-active, there's weights coming in, and those weights could be positive or negative.
cues.zh: 啟動或未啟動的概念，而是傳入的權重，可以是正值或負值。

cues.en: If the sum of those weights is greater than zero, we'll go ahead and fire off a signal.
cues.zh: 如果這些權重總和大於零，就發出訊號。

cues.en: If it's less than zero, we won't do anything.
cues.zh: 小於零，就不做任何事。

cues.en: It's just a slight adaptation to the concept of an artificial neuron, where we're introducing weights instead of just simple binary ON and OFF switches.
cues.zh: 這只是稍微調整人工神經元概念，引入權重，取代簡單的二元開關。

cues.en: Let's build upon that even further, and create something called the perceptron.
cues.zh: 再進一步，建立所謂的感知器。

cues.en: A perceptron is just a layer of multiple linear threshold units.
cues.zh: 感知器，就是由多個線性門檻單元組成的一層。

cues.en: Now we're starting to get into things that can actually learn!
cues.zh: 現在開始進入真正能學習的東西。

cues.en: By reinforcing weights between these LTU's that produced the behavior we want, we can create a system that learns over time how to produce the desired output.
cues.zh: 強化 LTU 之間，能產生所需行為的權重，就能建立一個隨時間學習、產生所需輸出的系統。

cues.en: This is also working more toward our growing understanding of how the brain works.
cues.zh: 這也更符合我們日益增加的大腦運作知識。

cues.en: Within the field of neuroscience there's a saying that "cells that fire together wire together," and that's speaking to the learning mechanism going on in our artificial perceptron,
cues.zh: 神經科學有句話：「一起放電的細胞，會連在一起。」這描述的正是人工感知器中的學習機制，

cues.en: where we have weights that are leading to the desired result that we want.
cues.zh: 也就是有些權重，會帶來我們想要的結果。

cues.en: We can think of those weights as strengths of connections between neurons, we can reinforce those weights over time, and reward the connections that produce the behavior that we want.
cues.zh: 可以把權重想成神經元連接的強度，隨時間強化權重，獎勵產生所需行為的連線。

cues.en: You can see here we have our inputs coming into weights just like we did in LTU's before, but now we have multiple LTU's grouped together in a layer.
cues.zh: 這裡的輸入，一樣先經過權重，像先前 LTU 那樣，但現在有多個 LTU 組成一層。

cues.en: Each one of those inputs get wired to an individual neuron in that layer.
cues.zh: 每個輸入，都接到那一層中的個別神經元。

cues.en: We then apply a step function to each one, which will produce a final set of outputs that can be used to classify something, like what kind of image this perceptron is looking at.
cues.zh: 接著對每個套用階躍函數，產生最後一組輸出，可用來分類，例如辨認感知器看到的是哪種影像。

cues.en: Another thing we introduce here is something called the Bias Neuron off there on the right.
cues.zh: 這裡另一個新增的東西，是右邊的偏差神經元。

cues.en: It's something to make the mathematics work out; sometimes we need to add in a little fixed constant value to make the neurons fire at the right values, and this bias amount can also be learned
cues.zh: 它是讓數學運算成立的東西；有時需要加入一個小的固定常數，讓神經元在正確數值放電，而這個偏差量，也能在

cues.en: as the perceptron is trained.
cues.zh: 訓練感知器時學習。

cues.en: So, this is a perceptron.
cues.zh: 這就是感知器。

cues.en: We've taken our artificial neural network, moved that to a linear threshold unit, and now we've put multiple linear threshold units together in a layer to create a perceptron.
cues.zh: 從人工神經網路，到線性門檻單元，再把多個 LTU 放在同一層，建立感知器。

cues.en: Now we have a system that can actually learn as you optimize all of the weights between the neurons in each layer, and you can see there's a lot of those weights at this point which can capture fairly complex information.
cues.zh: 現在，只要最佳化每層神經元之間的所有權重，系統就能學習；可以看到，此時已有很多權重，能捕捉相當複雜的資訊。

cues.en: If you have every one of those inputs going to every single LTU in your layer, they add up fast, and that's where the complexity of deep learning comes from.
cues.zh: 如果每個輸入都接到該層的每個 LTU，連線數很快增加，深度學習的複雜性就來自這裡。

cues.en: Let's take that one step further, and we'll have a multi-layer perceptron.
cues.zh: 再進一步，建立多層感知器。

cues.en: So now instead of a single layer perceptron of LTU's, we're going to have more than one.
cues.zh: 現在，不只有一層 LTU 感知器，而是多層。

cues.en: We actually have now a hidden layer in the middle there.
cues.zh: 中間確實多了一個隱藏層。

cues.en: You can see that our inputs are going into a layer at the bottom, the outputs are layered at the top, and in between we have this hidden layer of additional LTU's, linear threshold units,
cues.zh: 可以看到，輸入進入底層，輸出在頂層，中間是更多 LTU，也就是線性門檻單元構成的隱藏層，

cues.en: that can perform what we call Deep Learning.
cues.zh: 能執行所謂的深度學習。

cues.en: So here we already have what we would call today a Deep Neural Network.
cues.zh: 這裡已經是今天所說的深度神經網路。

cues.en: Now there are challenges of training these things because they are more complex, but we'll talk about that later on.
cues.zh: 因為更複雜，訓練有一些挑戰，稍後再談。

cues.en: The thing to really appreciate here is just how many connections there are, so even though we only have a handful of artificial neurons, you can see there's a lot of connections between them
cues.zh: 這裡真正要體會的是，連線有多少。即使只有少數人工神經元，也能看到大量連線，

cues.en: and there's a lot of opportunity for optimizing the weights between each connection.
cues.zh: 每個連線的權重，都有很大的最佳化空間。

cues.en: So that's how a multi-layer perceptron works.
cues.zh: 這就是多層感知器的運作。

cues.en: You can see that again we have emergent behavior here.
cues.zh: 再次看到湧現行為。

cues.en: An individual linear threshold unit is a pretty simple concept, but when you put them together in multiple layers all wired together, you can get very complex behavior because there's a lot of different possibilities
cues.zh: 單個線性門檻單元概念很簡單，但把它們以多層連在一起，就能產生非常複雜的行為，因為各種連線之間的

cues.en: for all the weights between all those different connections.
cues.zh: 所有權重，有非常多不同可能性。

cues.en: Finally, we'll talk about a modern Deep Neural Network.
cues.zh: 最後，談談現代深度神經網路。

cues.en: Really this is all there is to it; the rest of this section will just be talking about ways of implementing something like this.
cues.zh: 其實全部就是這樣，這一節其餘部分，只是談如何實作類似的東西。

cues.en: So all we've done here is replace that step function with something better.
cues.zh: 這裡所做的，只是用更好的函數，取代階躍函數。

cues.en: We'll talk about alternative activation functions; this one is illustrating something called ReLU, which we'll examine more deeply very soon.
cues.zh: 會介紹其他激活函數，這裡畫的是 ReLU，很快就會深入研究。

cues.en: The key point is that a step function has a lot of nasty mathematical properties, especially when you're trying to figure out their slopes and their derivatives, so turns out that other functions work out better
cues.zh: 重點是，階躍函數有很多麻煩的數學性質，尤其計算斜率、導數時，因此其他函數更好用，

cues.en: and allow you to converge more quickly when you're trying to train a neural network.
cues.zh: 讓訓練神經網路更快收斂。

cues.en: We'll also apply softmax to the output, which we talked about in the previous lecture.
cues.zh: 也會對輸出套用前一堂談過的 softmax。

cues.en: That's just a way of converting the final outputs of our neural network or deep neural network into probabilities from which we can just choose the classification with the highest probability.
cues.zh: 它只是把神經網路或深度神經網路的最終輸出，轉成機率，再選機率最高的分類。

cues.en: And we will also train this neural network using gradient descent or some variation thereof.
cues.zh: 也會使用梯度下降，或其某種變形，訓練神經網路。

cues.en: Maybe that will use autodiff, which we also talked about earlier, to actually make that training more efficient.
cues.zh: 也許使用前面談過的自動微分，讓訓練更有效率。

cues.en: So that's pretty much it!
cues.zh: 大致就是這樣。

cues.en: In the past five minutes or so that we've been talking I've given you the entire history of deep neural networks and Deep Learning.
cues.zh: 在剛才大約五分鐘，我已經介紹了深度神經網路與深度學習的整段歷史。

cues.en: It's not that complicated!
cues.zh: 沒那麼複雜。

cues.en: That's really the beauty of it.
cues.zh: 這正是它美妙的地方。

cues.en: It's emergent behavior; you have these very simple building blocks, but when you put these building blocks together in interesting ways, very complex and sometimes mysterious things can happen.
cues.zh: 這是湧現行為：基本元件非常簡單，但以有趣方式組合，就會發生非常複雜、有時神祕的事情。

cues.en: Let's dive into more details on how it actually works up next.
cues.zh: 接著，更詳細看看它實際如何運作。
